notes: kb/Work PB5130 owns the fix. §1989:A.2.17.3 AR1 bounds the year below only ("It must be an integer greater than 1600."); 2023 adds "and less than 10000". The runtime body IntegerOfDay refuses a year above 9999 at every edition ("year is < 1601 or > 9999" returns the argument-error value 0), so at --std 85 INTEGER-OF-DAY (10000001) returns 0 where the 1989 value is 3067672. The rest of the rule conforms: the integer screen (CheckArgumentClasses, IntegerViolation) refuses a non-integer or non-numeric argument, and the body checks DDD against the year's length ("a positive integer less than 367 provided that it is valid for the year specified": 1604366 gives 1461). The witness runs 1601001 and 1602001 only.

next.reason: 1985: "It must be an integer greater than 1600."; 2023: "It shall be an integer greater than 1600 and less than 10000.". 2023 adds an explicit upper bound on YYYY (less than 10000) that the 1985 text does not state; the YYYYDDD form and the DDD rule are otherwise the same.
